task: Fix the OOM crash in the report generator after the result set size was not bounded.

candidate_memories.content: Report generator crashes with OOM when generating reports for enterprise accounts with more than 500,000 records.
The report generator must use streaming with a page size of 1,000 records instead of loading the full result set.
The original generator loaded all records into memory; streaming was planned but never implemented.
Standard accounts with under 10,000 records are not affected; only enterprise accounts trigger the OOM.
Session 2 note: an enterprise customer filed a support ticket reporting report generation crashing with an out-of-memory error.
The report generator is a Go service with a 512MB memory limit set by Kubernetes.
Session 5 note: the finance team requested a new report format for quarterly reconciliation.
Old lesson: in-memory processing was used for reports before enterprise account sizes exceeded memory limits.
Enterprise accounts represent 15% of accounts but 60% of data volume.
Session 10 note: the performance team profiled the report generator and found heap growth with large result sets.
Old report guide: the 1,000-record page size was used in the search service but not adopted for reports.
Data processing services must use streaming or pagination for result sets that can exceed available memory.
Session 7 note: a new report type for monthly SLA compliance was added for enterprise accounts.
Report artifacts are stored in S3 and a download link is sent to the requester via email.
Session 3 note: the report generation timeout was increased from 5 minutes to 15 minutes for enterprise.
Reports are generated asynchronously; users receive a notification when the report is ready.
Memory limits must be tested against the maximum expected data volume before deploying to enterprise customers.
Session 12 note: a caching layer was added for frequently requested standard account reports.
Old generator config: the Kubernetes memory limit was 256MB before it was doubled for enterprise workloads.
The report generator uses a dedicated PostgreSQL read replica to avoid impacting the application database.
